findings.title: Webhook delivery-id cache could be poisoned via invalid timestamp
findings.evidence: In packages/webhooks/src/github.ts the handler adds the x-github-delivery value to processedDeliveryIds synchronously at the top of the route (before any await). If the x-github-delivery-timestamp / x-hub-timestamp header is non-numeric, the handler returns 401 at the 'Invalid timestamp' branch without deleting the in-flight marker. An attacker who knows or can predict a future GitHub delivery UUID can therefore suppress that legitimate delivery for the lifetime of the process.
findings.fix: Added processedDeliveryIds.delete(deliveryId) on the invalid-timestamp validation-rejection path, consistent with the missing-signature, invalid-signature, invalid-JSON, non-pull_request-event, and unsupported-action paths.
findings.test_evidence: Extended packages/webhooks/src/__tests__/github-webhook-idempotency.test.ts with 'does not let an invalid-timestamp request poison the delivery id cache', which sends a signed request with timestamp 'not-a-number', asserts 401, then sends a valid signed request with the same delivery id and asserts 200 with createPrReview called exactly once.

findings.scope: out-of-scope / pre-existing design accepted in Phase 3
findings.title: Process-local processedDeliveryIds Set grows unbounded for valid deliveries
findings.evidence: Valid delivery IDs are never removed from the in-memory Set in packages/webhooks/src/github.ts or packages/domain/src/codecamp/pr-reviews.ts. In a long-running production process under high webhook volume this is a slow memory leak, although each entry is small (a UUID string).
findings.fix: Not fixed in Phase 3 to stay within the representative-slice scope. Wave 4's webhook retry/DLQ track should move durable dedup fully to Postgres and bound or TTL the in-memory window.
findings.test_evidence: N/A — pre-existing/accepted design, no new tests added.

findings.title: 500 processing failures suppress same-process GitHub retries
findings.evidence: The outer catch in packages/webhooks/src/github.ts returns 500 without deleting processedDeliveryIds, so a GitHub retry hitting the same process is suppressed until restart. This matches the Phase 3 design intent of treating a delivery that passed validation as a duplicate even if mid-flight processing fails, and the inner runReview catch already persists a 'Review failed' status.
findings.fix: Not changed in Phase 3. Wave 4's Postgres-backed retry/DLQ track is the planned durable solution for processing failures.
findings.test_evidence: N/A — accepted design, no new tests added.

verified_controls.control: TenantDB unscoped() safety for REFERENTIAL codecamp tables
verified_controls.notes: Every unscoped query is scoped by an owner/resource key: userId, reviewId FK chain, prUrl, repoUrl, moduleId, exerciseId, or deliveryId. No unscoped REFERENTIAL query reads without a scoping predicate.
verifyWebhookSignature uses crypto.timingSafeEqual for constant-time comparison, requires GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET, and enforces a timestamp-replay window.
Two-layer dedup: synchronous in-process Set at route entry plus durable SELECT-before-INSERT in logWebhookEvent. All validation-rejection paths now release the in-memory marker.
HTTP 200 ACK is returned before the background review promise resolves; failures are persisted via updatePrReview inside runReview's catch.
Matched GitHub login is mapped to a user context with hardcoded INTERN role and the matched user's id; no privilege escalation path exists.

verified_controls.control: Chat route authentication and SSE framing
verified_controls.notes: Route calls requireAuth and returns 401 on auth failure. Error responses are generic; stack traces are logged server-side only. Response is reframed with text/event-stream Content-Type for client compatibility.
